title: Cancellation Charges by Contract Status
content:
# Cancellation Charges by Contract Status

Window Replacement Contracts — contract terms for a cancellation outside the cooling-off right.

**Rule.** A cancellation that does not qualify for the cooling-off terms is settled by the contract status on the date the written notice is given. In status signed the charge is the series pre-measure cancellation fee; in status measured it is the series measure-and-design charge; in status ordered it is the series product share of the adjusted contract value, which is the signed contract price plus the net contract charges (change orders and fees, less price credits) before the cancellation charge itself. A contract that is installed or closed cannot be cancelled; the customer's remedies after installation run through the service and warranty terms. The charge is booked as one cancellation charge fee on the notice date. Payments received (net of refunds) are kept up to the charge; the excess is refunded as a cancellation refund within the refund window, taken from the most recent payments first, each refund naming its source payment. When payments received are below the charge, the difference stays owed. Once a contract is cancelled, no further change order, measure visit, or price credit other than an on-time guarantee credit already earned is booked to it.

The product share is a share of the adjusted contract value, rounded to the cent.

## Charge by status on the notice date

| Status on the notice date | Charge |
|---|---|
| Signed | Series pre-measure cancellation fee |
| Measured | Series measure-and-design charge |
| Ordered | Series product share of the adjusted contract value |
| Installed or closed | Cannot be cancelled |

## Worked example, ordered contract (hypothetical inputs)

A hypothetical ordered contract has a signed price of $20,000, net contract charges of $1,000, and payments received net of refunds of $15,000, in a series with a hypothetical product share of 50%. The adjusted contract value is $21,000; the charge is $10,500.00 (50% of $21,000). Payments of $15,000 exceed the charge by $4,500, which is refunded, drawn first from the most recent payment and then from earlier ones, each refund naming its source payment.

## Payments below the charge (hypothetical)

A contract cancelled while measured, with a hypothetical charge of $400 and payments received of $250, keeps the $250 and the remaining $150 stays owed.
